description: FAST d=64 sweep (bf16, hstu) — small, shape-agnostic, no --filter needed, everything compiles for d=64. Two families collapsed from one axis product by the instance_gen gates: (1) BASE-TILE: max_k {64,96,128} x mtile {64,128} x use_splitkv {false,true} (split-KV needs mtile=64) at the dispatch-default WarpK = 9 kernels, incl. the HEUR baseline jagged_bf16_causal1_maxk64_mtile128_splitkv0; (2) a LIGHT TILE-SHAPE family pinned to the proven d=64 winner sequence<192,32,32,64,32,64> (km0=192,kn0=32,kn0sub=32,kn1=64,kk1=32) at the dispatch-default WarpK=16 (warp_k=0, 16x16x16 — the geometry the deployed example binary launches via try_run_tuned_jagged_forward /*WarpK=*/16 /*KN0=*/32, verified BIT-EXACT vs the maxk128 reference), max_k=64, non-splitkv, crossed with mtile {64,128} = 2 kernels, incl. the WINNER jagged_bf16_causal1_maxk64_mtile64_splitkv0_km0192_n032_n0s32_n164_k132. NOTE: warp_k=32 (16x16x32, the `_wk32` variant) is intentionally EXCLUDED here — it is faster but numerically BROKEN (149 sign-flip mismatches vs the maxk128 reference), so it must never be labeled BEST. The tile axes are {0,X} per dim; instance_gen gates make this honest and all-compiling: tile dims are all-or-nothing, warp_k=32 REQUIRES a tile (so base kernels keep default WarpK), tile overrides are restricted to max_k=64, and the existing tile-consistency gates apply (kn0sub==kk1, kn0%kk1==0, max_k%kn1==0, kk1>=warp_k). expand_sweep reads only data_type/use_causal/max_k/mtile/use_splitkv/km0/kn0/kn0sub/kn1/kk1/warp_k; silently-ignored knobs (pipeline/agpr/pingpong/trload/occupancy/num_splits) are not present. Expands to 11 kernels. For the full tile grid use sweep_exhaustive.json. Pass the shape inline, e.g. --batch 120 --num-head 4 --seqlen 16384 --hdim 64 --target-size 300.
